newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called up on cash, nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called up on cash, nuke outage.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Wednesday following Tuesday's late rally and news that a nuclear unit tripped off line in Louisiana, industry sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.33 to $2.35 after settling to the upside Tuesday at $2.309 per million British thermal units.
In ACCESS, June last traded 0.1 cent higher at $2.310.
"There was a little pullback last night in ACCESS. They're just using any excuse to move higher," one trader said, referring to the outage at Entergy Corp's River Bend plant.
The 936 megawatt River Bend nuclear unit is expected to remain shut for one to two weeks for repairs.
Also boosting futures were early cash prices at the Henry Hub, La., in the low-to-mid $2.30s, indicating a gain of at least five cents from Tuesday.
Technically, traders pegged resistance in June at the $2.385 contract high. Support was first seen at $2.20, with major buying likely at $2.05 and then along the up trendline around $2.03.

In Tuesday's cash market, Gulf Coast swing prices rose another two cents to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas firmed about five cents to the low-$2.50s.
Expectations for today's weekly AGA inventory report are about 25-70 bcf of injections, versus a gain of 53 bcf a year ago.
